name: Nationalism
summary: Nationalism holds that nations are real, valuable communities whose members are entitled to govern themselves, ideally in a state matching the nation. It prizes a shared culture, language and memory and gives the national community a special claim on loyalty. Strands differ on whether the nation rests on ancestry (ethnic) or shared political membership (civic) and on economic and social questions.
scope: The mainstream family as documented by Herder, Mazzini and Renan and in the Stanford Encyclopedia and Wikipedia: nation-centered self-determination with civic and cultural strands. It does not take the extreme ethnic, fascist or expansionist strands as the typical adherent, and many answers on issues outside nationhood are 0 because the ideology is not a full program.

sources.usedFor: Protectionism, state direction of the economy and immigration concerns.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Statist nationalism links shared culture to welfare, while others do not, so adherents split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Economic nationalism holds markets should serve national goals.

public-ownership.rationale: Economic nationalists often accept state ownership of strategic sectors but it is not definitional.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are supported by some nationalists and restrained by others.

property-fundamental.rationale: Nationalists split between liberal, socialist and statist economic views.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Economic nationalists favor regulation in the national interest but liberal nationalists differ.

cut-welfare.rationale: Split between statist and conservative strands.

worker-ownership.rationale: Mazzini favored cooperative association of labor but the wider family has no position.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security-minded strands favor it, liberal ones oppose; no settled position.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No nationalist position on this issue.

strong-leader.rationale: Authoritarian nationalisms favor strong leaders, while liberal nationalism does not.

state-harmful.rationale: Nationalism seeks a state for the nation, so a stateless order is contrary to its core.

empower-police-military.rationale: Security-oriented strands favor it, civic strands are indifferent.

decide-locally.rationale: Nationalists favor national self-government, which can pull against both local autonomy and central power.

traditional-family.rationale: Conservative nationalists treat inherited identity and family continuity as valuable, inferred and not universal.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Split by strand and country, with no core nationalist position.

abortion-legal.rationale: Split by strand and country; some nationalists favor higher birth rates, others are liberal.

more-religion-public.rationale: Some nationalisms are closely tied to a national church while liberal and secular ones are not.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a defining nationalist issue and adherents are split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Shared culture, language and inherited memory are what Herder, Renan and Mazzini treat as constitutive of a nation, so preserving them is central.

gradual-change.rationale: Conservative nationalists favor inherited institutions while liberal and revolutionary nationalists seek rapid change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Modern economic and cultural nationalists link immigration to dilution of national identity, but civic strands accept absorption of newcomers.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalism prizes national self-government free of outside interference and is often set against globalism.

free-trade.rationale: List-style economic nationalists favour protecting national industry, while Mazzini-era liberal nationalists supported free trade among nations; the in-scope family does not take one position.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalism gives the nation special priority, though liberal strands such as Mazzini hold that nations should cooperate as equals.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents divide between sovereignty and solidarity among peoples.

open-borders.rationale: Borders mark the nation self-governing units, so eventual abolition conflicts with the nationalist premise, though Mazzini hoped for harmony among nations.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy independence appeals to some nationalists but no settled position.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nationalist movements from the Risorgimento to anti-colonial struggles have justified rebellion to win national self-government.

experts-over-public.rationale: Popular sovereignty places authority in the nation, not in experts.

central-planning.rationale: Economic nationalists accept heavy state direction but do not usually endorse central planning.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism favors protecting domestic industry through tariffs, following List. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Economic nationalism holds that markets should serve national goals, which implies state direction, but the general nationalist family does not insist on it.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Mazzini valued equal rights and labor but nationalism has no settled property model.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not a nationalist aim; inferred from the absence of any such program.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Economic nationalists favor state control of economic levers, inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Fascist-era nationalism adopted corporatism, mainstream nationalism has no settled view.

one-party-rule.rationale: Mazzini asks that laws express the will of the whole nation, though some 20th-century nationalist regimes ruled by single parties.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Some nationalisms are monarchist and others, like Mazzini, republican.

democracy-best.rationale: Nationalism arose with popular sovereignty and the nation as the source of political power, though authoritarian nationalisms exist.

direct-votes.rationale: Nationalists favor popular will but have no settled view on direct versus representative democracy.

workers-councils.rationale: Nationalism places authority in the national assembly, not class councils, inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Self-determination is core, but the scholarship notes it does not automatically entail independence and many nationalists prefer devolution.

natural-rulers.rationale: Mazzini rejects privileges of inheritance and force, and recognizes only freely followed genius joined with virtue.

political-violence-never.rationale: Mazzini asks for readiness to take up arms for a people liberty, and nationalist movements have used force.

war-builds-character.rationale: Aggressive nationalisms glorify war, while Mazzini and Renan do not.

separate-church-state.rationale: Renan excludes religion as a criterion, but religion has been tied to nations such as Spain and Russia, so adherents are split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Mainstream nationalism grounds law in the national will rather than scripture, though religious nationalisms differ.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defence of the nation is a public task, inferred from the nation-state premise.

military-superiority.rationale: Aggressive nationalisms stress military strength, inferred as a common but not defining position.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Ethnic nationalism defines the nation by ancestry, while civic nationalism and Renan reject race as the basis, so adherents are split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalism puts the nation, not class, at the center of politics; Mazzini sought harmony across classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: No settled nationalist position; Mazzini sought equal rights but not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous self-determination echoes nationalist logic but conflicts with territorial claims of existing nation-states.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-colonial nationalists support them while others of the family do not, so inferred as split.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nationalism makes the nation, not a wider civilization or religion, the political unit; Renan says religion does not determine nationhood.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Mazzini and Renan stress duty and sacrifice for the community over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Mazzini made duties to country and humanity the foundation of rights, and Renan describes the nation as demanding sacrifice.

limit-population.rationale: No nationalist position; some favor population growth for national strength.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Economic nationalists prize industrialization as a source of strength and autonomy.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Popular and national self-government sits poorly with ceding decisions to algorithms, inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Nationalists often invoke a national past but many pursue progress and liberty.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Nationalism is itself a guiding principle, inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Mazzini favored insurrection and associations but nationalist movements also use elections.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nationalism presupposes organized nations and states, which foraging rejects.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Mazzini describes nations as a common workshop with divided tasks; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Nationalists see class cooperation within the nation, not exploitation, inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Mazzini opposes class rule and asks laws to express the will of the whole nation.

collective-farming.rationale: No nationalist program of this kind, inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Nationalism locates conflict in the clash of nations rather than capitalism, inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Citizens owe duties and sacrifice to the nation per Mazzini and Renan.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nationalism treats the nation as a group with collective claims to self-determination, so rights are not only individual.

conscription.rationale: Citizen armies and readiness to defend the country are common nationalist themes; inferred from Mazzini and the historical record.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nationalism ties members to a common country and stresses voice and belonging.

state-as-business.rationale: A nation is a community of memory and duty, not a business, per Renan.

media-academia-power.rationale: Populist nationalists claim this, others do not.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Renan explicitly denies that race makes a nation, though ethnic strands have claimed racial differences.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist nationalisms favor it, liberal nationalism does not.

total-state.rationale: Totalitarian nationalisms exist, but the mainstream family does not demand state direction of all life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rebirth themes appear in Risorgimento and later fascist nationalism, but the mainstream does not require radical renewal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Mazzini calls conquest a corruption of the natural division of nations and Renan rejects strategic claims over populations, though irredentist strands differ.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on the national community, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Mazzini calls for equal rights and freedom from privilege.

universal-morality.rationale: Mazzini grounds duties in God and humanity, while Herder-style nationalism stresses cultural particularity.

single-common-good.rationale: Nationalism posits a national interest but not a single rationally derived good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Applying national self-determination to Jews as a people, Zionism is a nationalism; other nationalists generally accept the principle but not all. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Irredentist and ethno-cultural strands count diaspora members as part of the nation, but this is inferred and civic strands differ.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language is treated since Herder as central to national identity, and nationalist movements have often revived or promoted a national tongue.

school-vouchers.rationale: No nationalist position; national curricula are valued by some.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic nationalists subordinate markets to the state, liberal nationalists differ.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-determination of nations is the defining claim in Mazzini, Renan and the scholarship.

force-without-un.rationale: Nationalism puts a nation's self-rule and interests first and is wary of supranational authority, so adherents mostly resist needing outside approval; inferred from that, as the ideology has no settled position on military action.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Inferred from the SEP's account of national attachment as a sentiment of loyalty and shared memory rather than a conclusion of pure reason; civic strands like Renan's are more rationalist, so this is a weak lean.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Nationalism gives the national community a special claim, and economic nationalists favor citizens-first benefits, though civic strands accept absorbing newcomers; inferred from its priority on the nation.

positive-liberty.rationale: Nationalism is not a full economic program, and adherents split on whether freedom requires material means.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Nationalism does not address welfare design; civic and conservative strands differ, so this is inferred as split.

class-collaboration.rationale: Inferred: nationalism puts the national community above class, and Mazzini describes the nation as an association of equals rejecting privilege.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nationalism prizes shared culture and memory, and Renan names the inherited past as the basis of the nation, so discarding its institutions runs against it.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-colonial nationalisms favored such fronts but others align with the West; adherents are split and the issue is not core.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalism is defined in part by opposition to internationalism and gives the national community priority over class solidarity across borders.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred: civic strands are egalitarian while conservative and ethnic strands favor distinct roles, so adherents are split.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred: mainstream nationalism does not call for banning interest, though some economic nationalists distrust finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The mainstream civic and cultural family rejects race as the basis of the nation, as Renan does, so legal racial separation is outside it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Inferred: nationalism sees the state as the expression of the nation, not as an instrument of a ruling class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Economic nationalists may favor energy self-sufficiency, but there is no settled nationalist energy position.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nationalism prizes shared culture and language, so adherents tend to expect integration, though civic strands stress political rather than cultural membership.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement thesis belongs to the ethnic fringe the scope excludes; mainstream civic and cultural nationalism does not hold it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Nationalism is silent on electoral systems; it concerns who the nation is, not how seats are allocated.

national-mission.rationale: Mazzini saw nations as equals and Renan rested the nation on consent, which sits poorly with imposing one's government on others, though some strands hold a civilizing mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Nationalism has no position on gender relations; adherents split along other lines.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Populist nationalists say yes while state-building nationalists defend national institutions, so adherents split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Renan rejected race as the basis of nationhood and mainstream nationalism is not eugenic; only extreme ethnic strands differ.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Nationalism does not address this directly; patriotic loyalty to the state's forces competes with demands for accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Economic nationalism holds that the state should direct the economy toward national goals, so a minimal state is disfavored.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Renan argued that race does not make a nation and that membership rests on shared will and memory; the mainstream strands the scope follows reject ancestry-based marriage rules.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Mazzini grounds national duty in the equal rights and duties of all people, though nationalism gives members of the nation a special claim on loyalty.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Inferred: national self-determination and economic nationalism favour national paths; the ideology has no direct position on this Marxist question.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred: nationalists split between those who see settlers' national claim as legitimate and those who see settlement as colonial.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred: civic nationalism stresses one shared citizenship under common law, while cultural strands may defend communal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred: cultural nationalists often tie religion to national identity and favour limits, civic strands defend religious freedom, so adherents split.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: the issue matters only to nationalisms tied to a sacred-animal tradition; most adherents have no common view.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred: some strands use schools to pass on national and religious heritage, others favour secular civic schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The statement concerns a socialist state, which nationalism as a general ideology does not address.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Renan's nation is a daily plebiscite and Mazzini ties nationhood to self-government, though ethnic strands rest legitimacy on the nation itself.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Nationalism is not a full program and the issue is not addressed in its core texts; adherents are split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalism favors protectionism and state direction of trade to strengthen the nation. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

population-transfer.rationale: Civic nationalists following Renan and Mazzini reject race-based exclusion, though ethnic strands have accepted population exchanges.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Mazzini rejects conquest and privilege, but nationalist movements have justified force for self-determination; inferred lean.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Mazzini sees nations as cooperating toward humanity, while ethnic strands see peoples as rivals; adherents are split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed by the core texts; adherents split between defending the nation's order and free political competition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Self-determination holds that a people ruled by outsiders is not free, matching the idea of freedom as not being under another's control.

separated-powers.rationale: Nationalism does not address how state power is organized; inferred indifference.

vanguard-party.rationale: Nationalism rests on the nation, not a class, and the mainstream works through national consent rather than a class vanguard; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Nationalism is indifferent to this economic question and strands differ.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Nationalism is not a full economic program, so adherents split on housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Nationalism takes no settled position on industrial action; adherents split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not an issue nationalism addresses; the strands differ, so this is inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Nationalists stress a shared culture and language as the basis of cohesion, though civic nationalists (Renan) accept pluralism; so a modest lean.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Nationalism favours self-government by the nation, usually through representative institutions; lotteries are not a nationalist concern.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Strands differ: statist nationalism accepts emergency powers, liberal civic nationalism does not.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: No settled nationalist position; economic nationalism favours state direction but varies on price controls.

party-controls-media.rationale: Civic nationalists such as Mazzini and Renan favour free expression, though statist strands differ; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Nationalism ties the army to the nation and state, not a party; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Nationalists treat citizenship as membership in a national community with shared culture, so a longer wait is the typical lean.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Nationalism has no position on official pay; adherents split, inferred from its being a program about nationhood rather than office.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Nationalist movements range from disciplined parties to loose coalitions, so adherents split; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Nationalism holds that nations should govern themselves, so pooling sovereignty in a binding supranational union is generally resisted, though civic nationalists accept some cooperation.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Nationalism is compatible with parliamentary and presidential systems alike; inferred from its focus on the nation, not on state structure.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Nationalism sees religion as a possible marker of national identity but takes no side on church governance; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Mainstream civic and cultural nationalism, as in Mazzini and Renan, grounds the nation in shared membership rather than clerical authority; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nationalism gives the national community a special claim on loyalty, and Mazzini and Renan treat duty to country as primary, so working for its defeat is opposed.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Mainstream liberal nationalists favor free expression, though conservative strands would censor; inferred as the majority view.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Nationalism has no settled view on term limits and adherents split by regime; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Nationalism does not address recall; civic strands rooted in popular consent might favor it but others would not; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Nationalism is about self-rule for nations, not a stance on alliances; nationalists split between wanting sovereign freedom of action and valuing alliances of nation-states.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Nothing in the doctrine bears on tenure, and most nationalist programs do not ban renting; inferred as mild disagreement, since the idea is not part of the mainstream program.

people-in-arms.rationale: Mazzini-style nationalism valued citizen levies for the nation's defense, but modern nationalists generally accept professional armies, so adherents are split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Herder-style cultural nationalism located the national spirit in the folk and the countryside; inferred as mild agreement, though many urban nationalisms exist.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nationalism's core claim is that state and nation should coincide, and Mazzini's unification program is the classic case; a nation split by an imposed border is a standard grievance.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist nationalism often disparages educated elites, but the mainstream tradition produced by intellectuals (Herder, Renan) does not; adherents are split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Herder held cultures to be distinct and each valuable, while nationalists also prize their own culture's achievements; adherents are split on ranking.

death-penalty.rationale: Nationalism takes no position on capital punishment; adherents vary with their wider politics.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The ideology is silent on school curricula about sex; nationalists range from conservative to liberal on it.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not a nationalist issue as such; nationalist movements split between religious traditionalists and secular ones.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not a defining issue; nationalists range from morally conservative to liberal on obscenity law.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnic strands favor descent and civic strands favor birthright or residence, as Renan's voluntary nation suggests; the mainstream is split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Minority nationalists want state support for their language while majority nationalists favor one national language as a unifier; the family is split.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not an issue the doctrine addresses; nationalists divide on whether a national culture leaves room for exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Cultural nationalism values shared customs and a common national culture, so mild disagreement is inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Nationalists stress national obligations and sovereign interests, and the mainstream core has no stance on debt; economic nationalists dislike creditors dictating terms but also honour national credit; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Nationalists value independence for its own sake, while economic nationalists want economic control; strands split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Self-determination and consent of the people, as in Renan and the Stanford entry, favour a nation making its own constitution through its elected representatives.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Mainstream civic nationalism ties legitimacy to consent and shared membership, but state-building nationalists have defended authoritarian development; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nationalism gives the national community a special claim on loyalty and Stanford discusses special obligations to compatriots, so duties to distant strangers are weaker; Mazzini however held duties to humanity.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nationalists favour national self-reliance in defence and sovereignty, so an independent deterrent fits; inferred from the emphasis on sovereignty.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Popular sovereignty is central to civic nationalism, so a head of state chosen by citizens fits; monarchist and parliamentary nationalists differ.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Economic nationalism favours state direction of the economy and national control of finance, so it is wary of independent central banks; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Refusing to trade historic land for peace is typical of irredentist nationalism, which the scope excludes; the civic and cultural core in the sources takes no position on territorial concessions.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Conservative nationalists stress property and tradition while statist and economic nationalists subordinate it to the nation; adherents split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The ideology is not a full programme and has no stance on the USSR; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not a nationalist concern; adherents divide along other ideological lines.

collective-defense.rationale: Nationalists value sovereignty over entanglement, but also defend allied nations; adherents split.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Renan grounds the nation in present consent and plebiscite, and the SEP discusses self-determination, so annexation without consent is illegitimate.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Strands differ: some nationalists make religion part of national identity and others have curbed churches in the national interest.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from nationalism's emphasis on the nation as a unified community that a head of state can symbolize.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Nationalism backs self-determination for nations but also the integrity of existing nation-states, so the SEP records adherents on both sides.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nationalism aims at one national community under common institutions; autonomy is accepted mainly for minority nations.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Renan and Mazzini ground the nation in people and consent, not dynastic divinity.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No nationalist tax doctrine; economic nationalism is mainly about trade and state direction.

character-from-environment.rationale: Civic strands stress shared culture and education while ethnic strands stress ancestry, so adherents split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from Mazzini's and Renan's nation of equals under popular consent; absolutist rulers are not the nationalist ideal.

space-expansion.rationale: No doctrine on space; national prestige favors it, while spending priorities at home oppose it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Nationalism is compatible with many constitutional forms and has no settled view.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream civic and cultural strands; leader worship belongs to fascist and authoritarian strands excluded from the scope.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Nationalism puts national unity above class division, so it does not centre class struggle; inferred from its stress on the shared national community.

land-redistribution.rationale: Nationalism has no settled agrarian program; land reform appears in some national movements and not in others.

refugee-return.rationale: National movements typically assert the right of their people to return to the homeland; inferred from the nation-centred claim to territory.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism is a documented nationalist strand, but the mainstream strand profiled here rests on self-determination, so adherents split.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Mainstream nationalism defines the nation by culture or shared membership, not by religious law; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress law for women is not part of the nationalist program and mainstream adherents are mostly secular or liberal; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Nationalism's emphasis on national sovereignty and opposition to internationalism tells against shared currencies; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-nationalist unions exist, but the focus on each nation's own state pulls the other way, so adherents split.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Nationalists accept cultural autonomy for minorities but ideally want a state matching the nation, so the answer is split; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Nationalism holds that a people is entitled to its own homeland, which tells against staying put as a minority; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalists stress culture, language and shared memory as forces in history rather than production alone; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is outside the nationalist program; no settled position.

no-bailouts.rationale: Economic nationalism favours state support for national industry and banks; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Civic nationalists accept constitutional limits while majoritarian nationalists do not, so adherents split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not part of the nationalist program; no settled position.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Economic nationalism is protectionist but the mainstream does not seek a total closed bloc; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Nationalism has no settled position on trade standards; protectionists may welcome them and others oppose.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral incentives are not a nationalist theme, though appeals to national duty exist; no settled position.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Nationalist movements have used both insurrection and electoral politics; inferred split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Mazzini's text rejects privilege and treats the nation as an association of equals.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalism prizes shared culture and memory, and the nation-centred teaching of history is a standard nationalist aim.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mazzini and Renan defend each nation governing itself, which rejects rule over other peoples, though some imperial nationalisms differed.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalism gives the nation a special claim on loyalty, and schools are a standard means of building it.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Nationalism has no program on this and civic and ethnic strands differ, so adherents split.

public-money-creation.rationale: Economic nationalism favours state direction of the economy and monetary sovereignty; inferred from that.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Nationalism is not an economic theory and has no stance on capitalist collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Irredentist and imperial-successor nationalisms favour it while self-determination nationalists reject it, so adherents split.

delink-world-market.rationale: Economic nationalists favour protection and self-reliance, but few call for full delinking; adherents split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Marxist question outside nationalism, which has no settled position.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Nationalism offers no doctrine on private discrimination, and strands differ.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Nationalism centres on the nation, not on rights guarantees; civic strands favour them and others do not.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the self-determination principle: treaties that split a nation against its will lack legitimacy, though states also value stable borders.

elective-rulers.rationale: Nationalism is not a full programme; Mazzini was republican but monarchist nationalists exist, so adherents are split.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from Renan's emphasis on the nation's collective will, which favours common decisions over individual veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The mainstream family has no settled doctrine on resisting rulers; Mazzini favoured it, others did not.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Nationalism is silent on the form of government; adherents have backed both monarchs and parliaments.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism is not a theory of animals, so adherents are indifferent.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism has no stated position on the use of animals.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from Mazzini's duties toward fellow countrymen and the solidarity of the nation, though stated mainly as mutual duty among equals.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Mazzini's Duties of Man makes serving one's country a duty; withdrawal from public affairs contradicts national solidarity.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed by nationalism, which is not a theory of culture and power.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism does not theorise how the ruling class keeps power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed directly; economic nationalism stresses national interest but does not adopt this world-systems thesis.

native-born-offices.rationale: Adherents are split: ethnic strands reserve offices for natives, while civic strands treat naturalised citizens as equals.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from national self-determination: each nation should take its own road, free from outside direction.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Economic nationalism favours domestic development and independence from foreign capital, per the Wikipedia entry. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism is a recognised nationalist strand, but the mainstream family is split and many accept existing borders.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Adherents are split: ethnic strands favour descent-based rule, while the mainstream civic and cultural strands do not.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism is not a theory of constitutional foundations.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream family; adherents differ, and extreme nationalists were themselves fascist.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism as a theory takes no position on this historical question.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the weight nationalism gives to national memory and heritage, though adherents disagree about condemned figures.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism is not a theory of gender.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism has no stated position on domestic violence.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from nationalist emphasis on distinct national cultures and self-rule, though Herder's cultural pluralism does not rule out shared standards.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Adherents are split; the armed forces served as a national symbol and guardian in some traditions, while Mazzini's republic subordinated them.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism has no stated position on unpaid care work.

filial-duty.rationale: Nationalism is not a full programme and has no doctrine on family duties.

office-by-exam.rationale: Nationalism has no position on how officials are selected.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism favours state protection of national industry, which supports blocking foreign takeovers. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Outside nationhood; adherents are divided on divorce law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Mazzini and Renan stress popular consent but give no rule on recall of representatives.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not a nationalist question and adherents are divided.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Nationalists generally accept private ownership; community land tenure is inferred as disfavoured.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from national self-government, which expects the nation through its elected body to control spending.

single-official-language.rationale: A shared language is a core marker of the nation in Mazzini and Wikipedia, though Renan rejects language as a criterion.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Economic nationalism and national attachment to the land favour restricting foreign ownership; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Outside nationalism and adherents are divided between civic and ethnic strands.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not a nationalist question; adherents are divided.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Nationalists support the self-determination of other nations but not necessarily arming insurgents.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Self-determination of every nation is central, and Mazzini and the SEP reject domination of one nation by another.

corporate-influence.rationale: Nationalists of both left and right resent elites that put private interests above the national community, but the ideology has no settled line on lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Protecting national sovereignty from outside influence follows from nationalism's self-government claim, though liberal nationalists would object to the means.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Nationalists worry about national continuity and tend to prefer native births to immigration, though this is inferred rather than a core doctrine.

residents-only-property.rationale: Protecting the national homeland is congenial, but nationalism has no settled position on local property rules.

job-guarantee.rationale: Economic nationalists favour state direction of the economy but job guarantees are not a shared nationalist demand.

democratic-peace.rationale: Mazzini and Renan hoped for peaceful cooperation among free nations, but nationalism as such makes no claim on democratic peace theory.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Nationalism holds that members owe special duties to their nation and its law, so a rejection of any general duty to obey sits poorly with it; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Respect for each nation's right to self-government implies non-interference in other nations' affairs, but adherents accept exceptions such as aiding oppressed nations.

industrial-unions.rationale: Nationalism has no position on how unions are organised.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mainstream nationalism as represented by Mazzini and Renan rejects hatred of minorities; conspiracy theories belong to extreme ethnic strands outside this scope.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Nationalism has no settled position on marriage law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Nationalists have no common line on freedom of information; the issue is outside the ideology.

local-production.rationale: Economic nationalists favour domestic production, but local rather than national production is not a nationalist theme.

informal-organisation.rationale: Nationalism places the nation in a permanent state with formal institutions, so loose informal groups are not its model; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Self-determination within a nation's own state and opposition to internationalism lead nationalists to favour the national constitution and courts.

religious-nation.rationale: Mainstream nationalists in Renan's tradition reject religion as the criterion of the nation, though conservative strands accept it.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Nationalism treats nations as equals with a right to self-rule, so ritual submission to a leading power runs against it; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: National solidarity favors pooling within the nation, while regional nationalisms want to keep their revenue; adherents split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The ideology is a theory of the nation, not of property; economic nationalists differ on common ownership.

defeat-communism.rationale: Many nationalists oppose communism but national-communist strands exist; the ideology has no fixed line.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Economic nationalism ranges from state direction to market policies, so no common view on service providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Nationalists often tie the national community to its religious tradition, so they tend to reject the view that religion is an illusion; contested among adherents.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Economic nationalism takes no settled view of capitalism as a historical stage; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The ideology does not address gender and economic structure; adherents split.

socialized-care.rationale: No settled nationalist position; statist nationalists back welfare provision while others do not.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Cultural nationalists value language purity while civic nationalists do not, so adherents split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the principle that national self-determination rests on consent and that obligations bind; contested for dominant nationalisms.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Mazzini and Renan make the nation the political community, not small communes with common property; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Statist nationalisms have promoted settlement in minority regions while liberal and civic strands reject it; adherents split.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Economic nationalism sometimes presents itself as a third course, but nationalists are not agreed on this.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Many nationalisms invoke an ancestral homeland, but Renan (s2) argues that historical and ethnographic arguments cannot override the present will of the people who live in a territory; the family is divided.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mainstream nationalism as scoped rejects this; denial belongs to extreme ethnic strands. Inferred from the scope.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Nationalism is not a full program and its adherents are split on this.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mazzini's nation is an association of equals, and Renan's rests on consent, which sits poorly with suppression; adherents in power have differed.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not an issue nationalism addresses; adherents range from secular to religious.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The ideology's core is national self-determination and Mazzini rejects conquest and privilege, so ruling peoples for the ruler's benefit contradicts it.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A matter of Islamic law that nationalism as such does not address.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Renan holds that religion does not define the nation, so legitimacy rests on the national community, not religious law; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Mazzini and Renan ground the nation in popular consent, but direct participation in workplaces and universities is not addressed; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Nationalism puts the nation first and has no settled view on this framework.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Outside the ideology's concerns; adherents split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Outside the ideology's concerns; adherents split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Nationalism has liberal and conservative strands and nationalists often claim to speak for the whole nation above party; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Economic nationalism backs state direction of capitalism rather than a critique of wage labor as alienating; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Renan rejects religion as the basis of the nation while the sources note immigration concerns among nationalists; adherents split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority comes from the nation and its members, though Mazzini linked the people's duty to God; contested.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents split between secular and religious-identity nationalism.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic nationalism favors state direction and protectionism, while other strands accept markets; no single position.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Nationalism holds that self-governing nations must be able to defend themselves.

rich-first.rationale: Mazzini rejects privilege and stresses the equality of national members, though economic nationalists accept uneven growth; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Sovereignty and independence from outside powers are core, which favors staying out of rival blocs, though nationalists sometimes seek alliances; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Mazzini and Renan grounded the nation in equals and consent, but monarchist nationalists exist, so the mainstream leans against inheritance only mildly.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Nationalism is not a full economic program; adherents on credit policy split between statist and market positions.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Economic nationalism stresses national sovereignty over economic policy, which points toward resisting lender-imposed conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Mazzini described the nation as an association of equals with equal rights, which cuts against wealth qualifications for voting.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The ideology is silent on the link between domination of women and nature, and adherents are indifferent.

reification.rationale: Nationalism offers no theory of market society's effect on social perception, so there is no characteristic position.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Nationalism does not address media ownership, and adherents range from free-market to statist.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: Mazzini's nation of equals and liberal strands favor common law over arbitrary rule, though authoritarian nationalists differ.

racial-franchise.rationale: Renan rejected race as the basis of nationhood and the mainstream strands are civic or cultural, though the ethnic strand dissents.

online-participation.rationale: Nationalism has no position on online political participation.

open-government-data.rationale: Nationalism has no characteristic position on publishing government records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Renan held that religion does not define the nation, so mainstream nationalists mostly oppose legal restrictions, though religious nationalists differ.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Renan rejected religion as a criterion of the nation, so shunning a minority's shops cuts against shared national membership, though some strands differ.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Nationalism is a theory of national self-rule and says nothing on how deliberation is organised; adherents split between representative and participatory forms, so 0 is inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Nationalists split: some treat national religion as a tradition to preserve, others favour modernising it; the sources do not address this, so 0 is inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Nationalism is a theory of the nation, not an economic program; strands range from economic nationalists to liberals, so no stance is documented.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Nationalism does not address military service by sexual orientation; the answer depends on the strand's social outlook, so it is left neutral.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Mainstream nationalists such as Mazzini and Herder treated religion as part of national life and duty, so state-led promotion of atheism is contrary to the tradition.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Nationalism assumes a state that secures the nation and its order; abolishing police is not a stated position. Inferred from its emphasis on national self-rule.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Nationalism seeks self-government by the nation as one community, which tends against guaranteed communal shares of power; inferred from the sources' account of national self-determination.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Nationalism takes no stated position on charity versus state aid; the strands divide on welfare, with some stressing national solidarity through the state.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism is about nationhood, not the structure of representation.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism is about nationhood, not the mechanics of voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the ideology is not a full program and adherents have no common position.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; religious office is outside the ideology and adherents differ by culture and faith.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism says little on family law and the strands differ from liberal to traditional.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Nationalism gives members of the nation a special claim, so many adherents reserve voting for citizens, though civic strands are more open.

rent-control.rationale: Economic nationalists protect domestic interests, but nationalism has no housing doctrine, so adherents split.

abolish-ip.rationale: Nationalism values cultural creativity as national heritage and economic nationalists protect domestic IP, so abolition is mildly rejected by inference.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Some nationalists, such as in Mazzini's tradition, favour civic education and youth organisation, but mainstream nationalism is divided.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nationalists split on nuclear basing, as some value national security and others national independence.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Nationalism prizes national sovereignty and self-rule, so foreign bases on national soil are mildly opposed.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Nationalists value national memory and often press for recognition of their own nation's suffering, though attitudes to others' differ.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Economic nationalism and nationalism more broadly have no settled position on income from work versus ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Nationalism holds that dying for the nation can be a duty, as in Mazzini's duties to country, so absolute rejection of killing in defence is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Nationalism emphasises shared culture and memory linking past and present; Renan's critique and constructionist scholarship note the myth, but adherents mostly affirm continuity. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Nationalism has no position on sex and gender, so adherents split.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Nationalism has no position on feminist theory, so adherents split.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Nationalism honours those who die for the nation; Renan treats sacrifice as the heart of the nation, and Mazzini's duties extend to sacrifice.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Mazzini's religious nationalism treats the nation as a sacred mission, but civic strands are secular, so adherents split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Nationalism has no settled position on the role of diaspora versus gathering, as the statement concerns a particular case.

culture-before-state.rationale: Herder's cultural nationalism puts a people's language and culture first, as the SEP notes for cultural nationalists, though political strands put the state first. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

god-not-male.rationale: Nationalism has no position on religious language, so adherents split.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Nationalism has no position on judging religious texts, so adherents split.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Economic nationalists favour national priority, but civic nationalists reject ethnic preference, so adherents split.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Nationalism seeks a state for each nation, which suggests unity of a people's lands, but civic strands reject it, so adherents split.

independent-unions.rationale: Nationalism is not a full economic program and has no stated view on union independence.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Nationalism has no view on what makes a society socialist.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Nationalism has no settled view on public ownership; economic nationalists favour state direction of strategic industries, others do not.

second-chamber.rationale: Nationalism has no view on legislative design.

municipal-property.rationale: Nationalism makes the nation the main community of ownership and loyalty; ownership by the local community alone is inferred as contrary to that.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Nationalism holds that sovereignty belongs to the nation, and Mazzini favoured a unified nation over federal fragmentation; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Nationalism has no view on wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Nationalism has no view on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Nationalism has no view on ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Nationalism has no view on financial privacy.

online-anonymity.rationale: Nationalism has no view on online anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: Mazzini ties individual duty to the nation while also treating members as equals; the sources do not settle the question.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Mazzini and Herder tie the nation to duty, tradition and a higher purpose; the statement is inferred from that.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: A nation-state with sovereignty vested in the national legislature is the usual nationalist ideal; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Nationalism has no view on genetically engineered crops.

dense-cities.rationale: Nationalism has no view on urban density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Renan rejects race as the basis of a nation, and Mazzini describes the nation as an association of equals; mainstream nationalism does not organise by race.

racial-pride.rationale: Renan treats a heroic common past and ancestors as the social capital of a nation; pride in ancestry is inferred from that, not racial pride as such.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Mazzini's Duties of Man rejects conquest and privilege, and mainstream nationalism seeks self-determination, not expansion.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Mazzini names a shared language and tradition as marks of a nation, and cultural nationalism after Herder treats language as central, though Renan dissents. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the aim of one self-governing national community, which sits badly with permanent separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Fear of outside powers is common in embattled nationalisms but is not part of the mainstream doctrine, so adherents split.

free-public-college.rationale: Nationalism has no settled position on tuition; it is outside the ideology's concern.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Nationalism has no settled position on environmental policy tools.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from Renan's view of the nation as an inheritance of memories handed on to later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nationalism is silent on gender and values in public life.

arms-reduction.rationale: Nationalists want secure nation-states, and adherents split between arms limits and strong national defence.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Nationalism does not address how diplomacy is conducted.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic nationalism favours domestic control over capital, including restrictions on its movement, though not every nationalist is an economic nationalist.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Nation-state sovereignty implies a state monopoly on force; inferred, not a defining doctrine.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Nationalism makes duty to the nation central, as Mazzini's duties towards your country, so refusing national wars is rejected.

collective-bargaining.rationale: No settled nationalist position; some strands favour corporatist labor, others do not.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Adherents are split on welfare design; nationalism is not a full economic program.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Economic nationalists favour national fiscal autonomy but have no common view on debt rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Economic nationalists favour protecting national economies but do not agree on favouring developing countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Nationalism seeks a state matching the nation and so values the national state rather than destroying it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Nationalism ties economy to national interest, not to open communal experimentation; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; adherents split.

sacred-nation.rationale: Mazzini treats country as a sacred duty and Renan calls the nation a soul and spiritual principle, though many adherents see it in practical terms. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

student-debt-relief.rationale: No nationalist position on student debt.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Nationalism stresses the unity of the national community, so it tends to reject the framing of one region as colonising another, though regional nationalists use it; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Nationalists differ between universalist and particularist views of human nature; not a defining question.

public-service-media.rationale: Some strands see public media as a carrier of national culture, others distrust it; adherents split.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Nationalism is not a religious doctrine; Renan holds religion is not the basis of a nation, so adherents are indifferent.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from economic nationalism's support for protecting domestic producers and food self-sufficiency.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from nationalist emphasis on national sovereignty and self-defence; the sources do not address nuclear arms.

workers-own-party.rationale: Nationalism places national unity above class division, so it favours broad national parties; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Nationalism is not a full programme and says nothing on this; strands differ on defending custom versus modernising.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Mazzini's nation is an association of equals that rejects privilege, which implies equal rights; inferred, as modern strands differ.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Language is central to many nationalisms, but nationalists differ on whether to unify or separate related varieties.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Nationalism takes no position on how pollution is regulated.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Nationalism has no settled view; conservative strands honour tradition while civic strands favour elected bodies.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Nationalism takes no position on this trade-off; strands pair it with both conservation and growth.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Criminal sentencing lies outside nationalism's core concerns.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: A shared national language is a core nationalist value, and nationalist immigration policy commonly expects newcomers to adopt it.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Nationalism is not a full program; economic nationalists tend to back labor, while others favor free markets, so adherents split.

voter-id.rationale: Nationalism ties political membership to citizenship, so requiring proof of citizenship to vote is inferred as mild agreement.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Cultural nationalists often give a national church a privileged role while civic nationalists favor equality, so strands differ.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Nationalism links democracy to popular sovereignty of the nation, which can mean more than procedure, but it takes no firm stance.

premarital-sex.rationale: Nationalism has no doctrine on sexual morality; culturally conservative and liberal nationalists differ.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; civic nationalists oppose shutdowns while state-centered strands accept them for order, so adherents split.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not an issue nationalism addresses; economic strands differ on welfare design.

women-suffrage.rationale: Mazzini's national self-rule extended to all members of the nation, and modern nationalists accept equal suffrage, though historical nationalists differed.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Nationalists tend to value religion as part of national culture and reject the claim; inferred, with secular nationalists dissenting.

race-social-construct.rationale: Civic nationalists treat nations and races as constructed while ethnic nationalists see ancestry as real, and the strands split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Nationalism has no position on state gender agencies; adherents split on active government in social policy.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Nationalism is a theory of nationhood, not of property; economic nationalists and liberal nationalists differ on how land and resources should be owned, so this is not an inference from its stated principles.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Nationalists value sovereignty and are wary of external judges, while liberal nationalists accept international law; the ideology itself does not settle it.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Nationalism is indifferent to scriptural doctrine, though some religious nationalists hold this view; adherents are split.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Nationalism does not address gender in self-government; the nation is treated as a community and adherents range from feminist to traditionalist.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Nationalists may defend their state against foreign attack, but economic nationalism is not committed to planned economies; adherents split.

indirect-election.rationale: Mazzini and Renan's nation rests on the active consent of its citizens, which is inferred to favour direct popular choice of leaders over delegate chains.

national-church-status.rationale: Cultural nationalists favour an established national church as part of national heritage while civic nationalists do not, so strands split.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Nationalists back self-determination for their own nation, but whether minorities inside a state get territorial autonomy divides the strands.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Renan's 'daily plebiscite' makes the will of the inhabitants the test of nationhood, which supports letting a disputed territory's people choose.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Nationalists often accept inherited borders to protect the nation-state but irredentist strands want to redraw them; adherents split.

simple-living.rationale: Nationalism takes no position on lifestyle or consumption; this is not a nationhood question.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Strands split between protecting a homeland's national character and equal membership for all citizens; the sources do not settle it.

equal-conscription.rationale: Nationalism usually values citizen service to the nation, but whether women are equally liable is not addressed and adherents split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Mazzini describes the country as a shared home whose land and tradition citizens have a duty to serve; the 'spiritual' framing is not universal.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The ideology says nothing on this; liberal and authoritarian strands would answer oppositely.

close-ties-china.rationale: Alignment with a great power is outside nationalism, and nationalists typically stress independence from any patron.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Irredentism and concern for co-nationals across borders are documented features of nationalism, though civic strands reject them.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: No settled nationalist position on resource ownership; inferred from the absence of any economic doctrine.

self-ownership.rationale: Nationalism claims special obligations to compatriots but says nothing about self-ownership; strands split.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: No nationalist position on consumption taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Statist nationalism links culture to welfare while others do not, so adherents split on targeting.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Nationalist movements often rely on a charismatic leader, but liberal nationalists defend parties; adherents split.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Economic nationalists favour state-favoured national firms while liberal nationalists do not; adherents split.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Some nationalists build the nation on a religion and others on civic membership, so the question divides them.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist concern to preserve national culture and tradition while keeping the state strong.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; liberal nationalists say yes and conservative nationalists often say no.

national-resource-control.rationale: Economic nationalism seeks national control over the economy and its resources against foreign ownership.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Nationalism has no doctrine on distributive justice; economic nationalists favour state intervention while others accept market outcomes, so adherents are split.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Economic nationalists may back taxes on global finance, while other nationalists oppose new taxes; nationalism takes no settled view.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Nationalism is not about racial advancement; civic and ethnic strands differ and adherents are split on this domestic debate.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Nationalists stress loyalty to the national state and its laws, though some appeal to a national or divine higher justice; inferred and contested.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Nationalism has no position on automation; economic nationalists worry about jobs while others welcome productivity; adherents are split.

multipolar-world.rationale: Nationalism holds that each nation should govern itself, which favours a world of many sovereign powers over one dominant power, as Mazzini's vision of free nations shows.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Nationalism has no theory of value, and its tie to national cross-class solidarity sits against the Marxian framing; inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Nationalism prizes love of country and national solidarity across classes, and Mazzini linked duty to country with the welfare and association of working people.

material-over-identity.rationale: Nationalism is itself an identity politics of the nation and rejects putting class interests ahead of national and cultural belonging; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Mainstream nationalism rejects communist one-party rule, though economic nationalists accept strong state direction of markets; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Every nation has the right to govern itself in its own state.
missingStatements.rationale: Self-determination of nations is the defining claim in Mazzini, Renan and the scholarship, and no existing statement captures it directly.

notes: Ethnic, civic, liberal, conservative, economic and expansionist strands answer many items differently; the profile follows the mainstream core and marks inferences as low confidence.
